## Design

### 2026-10-29: First I planned out the project. I want to have a small business card style board with a segmented display at the bottom. It could show live stats based on web requests (like github stars or some othe

**3h**

First I planned out the project. I want to have a small business card style board with a segmented display at the bottom. It could show live stats based on web requests (like github stars or some other cool statistic) or updating text with whatever data.

After searching for components, reading some datasheets, and some brief research, I decided on the following parts list:
- 1x Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32C3 (MCU)
- 2x Generic 0.56 inch Red 4 Digit 7 Segment LED Displays
- 1x MAX7219 chip (display driver)

I then created an approximate layout of the parts on a board, just to make sure the dimensions and proportions were about right and how I'd like:

![Rough layout plan](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/fe3b24c57a370c81f2c809020144817718d301a791d1ea539bdc3f006d2ea82e.png)

Finally, I setup KiCad to work with all the components I planned and made a simple schematic, just hooking up the microcontroller with the MAX7219 chip and the displays.

![schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/e13f2a3ad0cfa68713fe085056d07fb90ccd123711ae517e73debde4d94178df.png)

I wanna start the PCB layout before finalising the schematic, in case I want to make any changes or additions. Also, since I have so many extra GPIOs, it feels like a waste to not put them to some use. So, I'm considering adding a fancy capacitive slider using one of KiCad's footprint generators, looking something like this:

![slider](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/41b91022da2ea0b7991e612534cf3d922ea2869cade41d7301bef94a4ecb98b3.png)

### 2026-10-30: I did some boring work:

**2.83h**

I did some boring work:
- Found the Rset resistor on Robu and set up its footprint (After deciding on 30kΩ based on the MAX7219 datasheet)
- Set up the remaining 3D models needed

And then the interesting part. I rearranged the board layout more, finalised the layout (I think) and the board size and stuff. I also made the touch slider footprint with KiCad's footprint wizard. Then I attempted the routing, but I'm definitely going to redo it or at least make significant changes to it, since it's currently really messy. This layout is probably the most convoluted routing I've had to do in KiCad before, mostly because of the seemingly random pin definitions for the displays and the MAX7219 chip. I already scrapped and redid it partially a few times and rearranged the schematic in between too. The timelapse really doesn't do justice to the amount of back and forth I had to do.
![schematic](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/6b2bdd5c6cda32392318f1a54dbf2da954ca633053495ee01ca442a3d5e7c46f.png)
![routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/4267ae5a7aa603f030a438c26bddb6ba776c0e688fb658be9ae2a1139c77f151.png)

Hopefully next time I try routing the board I'll learn from my mistakes and improve (and by that I mean the copper gods won't curse me with having to use this many random vias again)

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/01cc2f07-4372-4b25-89cc-aa4790cbe740/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-31: First I did some research online and got some advice from the Slack to improve the routing. Then I rerouted the board again.

**2.22h**

First I did some research online and got some advice from the Slack to improve the routing. Then I rerouted the board again.

Before:
![Old routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/4267ae5a7aa603f030a438c26bddb6ba776c0e688fb658be9ae2a1139c77f151.png)

After
![New routing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/ec0bb62a36647cfab023bec2143c666a1e65329fab653ed081343289c3d3fbda.png)

You may have noticed I also moved the GND plane from F.Cu to B.Cu.

Then I added some graphics to the board. A dodeca logo on B.Silkscreen and a wordmark on B.Cu. The wordmark is actually a rule area keepout that excludes the zone fill. I had to add extra zone fills to create the isolated copper islands for the counters in the "d"s. That took a bit of figuring out.

This is what the final board looks like:

![With graphics](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/9254466ecd1ca45c3e5643be7516244d66b52e3eb3f16e52ed729df18228109f.png)

I'm still gonna add more silkscreen graphics to the board, so it's not completely done yet.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/abc4e7c7-58dd-4748-879b-3329161a8d35/video.mp4)

### 2026-11-01: Just adding some finishing touches to the PCB now. I decided on and added some text on F.Silkscreen, along with a QR code and a stylised wordmark. I spent some time calculating positions and distances

**1.25h**

Just adding some finishing touches to the PCB now. I decided on and added some text on F.Silkscreen, along with a QR code and a stylised wordmark. I spent some time calculating positions and distances and aligning each element to ensuring everything was distributed properly. I also rounded the Edge.Cuts. Now, the board looks like this:

![PCB](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/d1bf6319e0a0185fbe5edd789e132289badd1421db51b98d5abcbc217a78d481.png)

Then I added some images to the repo and generated the board's gerber files.

Next, I created the BOM for the project:

![BOM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/WlipWVmF6UnTGNkVVXdowr37dB4xoM3o/4bd63c059eba5638ca61aa2ade88bb749cfef1816257dce38fe82828591b8a77.png)

Since I especially picked really cheap components, I was able to get the total cost just under $30 including shipping. I only need 1 resistor, but Robu won't let me buy only one because its cost is too low, so I'm buying 10 instead (It only costs an additional $0.09).

Next, I'll write the README and some simple firmware.

### 2026-11-01: Last entry of week 4!

**4h**

Last entry of week 4!

First thing I did was make the firmware. It only handles the display right now and shows some dummy text to test it's working properly.

I discovered that I won't be able to use the standard touch sensing library because the XIAO ESP32-C3 doesn't actually support touch sensing. But, no need for panic, I don't have to switch microcontrollers, because I've found there *are* ways (albeit complex and with some downsides) to still have touch sensing using the chip's pull-up functionality. It's kinda hard to plan and design that right now though, since I can't test with the board at all. So, I'll do that in the build week.

Also, the firmware includes a segments dict for each possible character. I probably could've found a list online, but I wanted full control over the look of the letters. So, armed with some screenshots of [segmented displays from Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seven-segment_display_character_representations) and a diagram from [the datasheet](https://robu-prod-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/products/attachments/vhLsh0cFfzyxSN4LQugApwKgnfJNADV1g4lqE36g.pdf), I wrote it out it manually.
